title: Giving birth alone to her premature son
summary: Her neighbor Mrs. Garland went to phone the clinic while Nellie delivered the baby alone and kept him alive by spanking him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So there was an old lady who lived below me. Garland, her name was Mrs. Garland, lived below me, and it so happened that she was home that day. She worked also. And she was home, and I looked out the window, out my back bedroom window, and I saw her in the yard, and so I called her and told her. I asked her if she would come upstairs a little while, so she says, "Oh, yes, I'll be up in a minute." So she took her time and she finally came upstairs. And I told her, I said, "Look, I'm not feeling good. You know, I went downtown and I think I probably walked a little too much, because I was shopping for the baby, and because I'm going to, after the next two weeks -- this is my last two weeks at work and I plan to stay home after that and I don't want to have to be shopping or anything." And she says, "Well, just lie down and rest awhile." So I'd lie
down and I'd sit up and I'd lie down and I'd sit up and I'd go to the bathroom. Oh, I carried on, you know, never thinking that this was so close to happening.

And so finally, she said, "Well, maybe I should massage you." And she got the -- what did she get? She was supposed to get something that I had there to massage with. Instead of getting what she should have gotten she got some vinegar or something and was massaging me, and it was so cold. It's a good thing it was in June. My son was born the 15th of June.

I said, "Oh, my God, it's cold, it's cold." She apologized. She said, "Well, just lie down and just don't bother," she says. "Well, maybe I shouldn't bother you," she said. "I'll just sit here." We had twin beds and she sat on the other twin bed there, and so finally every once in awhile I'd get up and she said, "Oh, my God." I said, "You know, I have a feeling that I should let you call my doctor," and she says, "Who is your doctor?" And I said, "Well, I've been attending a clinic downtown," you know, and I said, "I think you should call them and let them know," you know, "that I'm having trouble, and maybe they can recommend or tell you something to do for me." She says, "Well, I'll do that."

Well, at that time we didn't even have a telephone, really. We didn't have our own phone, but we used to use the landlord's phone. He lived in the back, in the back of this apartment house. He owned the house in the back. So she said,

"Well, I'll go downstairs and call. I'll go to my house." So she went to her house, which was right below me, and she called and told them. I gave her my clinic card, and she got the clinic card and she gave them the number and everything. So they said, "Well, we have a doctor and a nurse out now. We will have them to come by and see about her. They're not too far from there and we'll just have them to come in and look in on her." And while this lady was down making this call, my son was born. He was born.

Yes. He was born, and strangely enough, he was almost born in the commode, because, you know, you keep running. Well, you know, you've had a child, so you know what. This water keeps coming. And I -- you know, you feel like every minute you want to do and you don't want to do, you know. When I got back to the bed, just got back to the bed in time, and I felt this awful thing happening, you know, something just coming, and here comes my son, here comes everything, well just everything. Well, the umbilical cord was broken. And I just don't know, I can't tell you where I got the -- I don't know what you would call it, the nerve or the whatever, the knowhow, that's the word I want to say, the knowhow to carry on or to do whatever needed to be done, but it had to be God in action.
Immediately after this all happened I was free. You understand what I'm saying, I was free of him, you know. And right outside of my bedroom -- it wasn't a big room -- was we

had an old refrigerator sitting there and on the top of this refrigerator we had newspapers and things like that, so I was able to -- by me being free, by this cord being broken, I was -- I'm sure that's why he was prematurely born, because the cord was broken -- and I was able to step outside of the room and get these papers and put the -- you know, to help cover up some of the goo that was there, and then my husband's robe was around, and I just wasn't worrying about whatever, whose was what, I just wanted to try to -- and my whole thing was to try to protect this baby, and he was so still and quiet I thought he was -- I didn't even think he was alive, you know.

So I used to hear my grandmother -- then I heard somebody talking about this on the radio the other day, about spanking babies when they're, you know, newly born babies -- I used to hear my grandmother talk about spanking babies and how they used to spank them, you know, when they were first born.

So I just happened to pat him on his little buttocks, you know, and when I did it the first time he moved a little bit, and then I did it the second time and he moved. Then after awhile I spanked him, and he started a little faint cry, and the more I spanked him the more he cried. He just (Imitating crying of baby). Then I got excited. I said, 'Oh, my God, I hope they hurry up so they can save him. And sure enough, in about, oh, -- it all happened so quickly, right now I have no idea, when I'm talking about time I can't even say how many
minutes or how long or anything. I haven't any idea as to how long it took. But -- because to me it's just like it happened yesterday, I can remember it so vividly.

This lady came, that woman who had gone to make the phone call, came back upstairs, and she was taking her own time, you know. Not intentionally, but she was just an older woman and she couldn't walk too fast. And she came back and said, "Oh, Mrs. Lewis, they will be here in a little while to see about you. They're in the neighborhood and they will be by to see about it." I said, "Come quick. Come quick. The baby is here." And she says, "Oh, no. No. Oh no, it can't be." So when she came up and saw this baby lying there, and I had him covered over, you know, and I wouldn't put it all the way over his face, just enough to keep him breathing, and I spanked him a little bit so she could hear him cry, and she said, "Oh, my God. Oh, what can we do." I said, "Well, we can't do anything. Let's not do anything. We'll just have to wait till they come." And I just spanked him and kept spanking him until they came.
